We want quarto.org to work for everyone. This page shows the results of an automated accessibility scan of the site. It is one input to that goal, not the whole of it. Automated tools find about a third of accessibility problems, so we also test by hand.

## How the scan works

Every week, a workflow renders the site and runs [`quarto call axe`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/pull/14815), an experimental Quarto command that checks every page with [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core). Each page is checked at a desktop and a phone viewport, and in light and dark mode where the page has both.

The scanner groups violations by root cause, so one entry below can cover many pages. A finding that repeats across the site usually comes from a shared template, and one fix clears it everywhere.

## Reporting a problem

If you find an accessibility problem on quarto.org, please [open an issue](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/issues/new). If the problem is in the HTML that Quarto produces, it belongs on [quarto-cli](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/new/choose) instead. Either is fine. We will move it if needed.
